title.en: Define mobility and use vd = μE

say.en: A drop of ink spreads through still water with no push at all. Charge carriers in a semiconductor can move that way too, or be pushed by a field. In this lesson: Distinguish drift and diffusion currents.
Define mobility and use vd equals micro E.
Calculate conductivity and resistivity of a doped sample.

body.en: When an electric field E is applied, holes *drift* along the field and electrons against it; both make current in the direction of E. The average drift velocity is proportional to the field: $v_d = \mu E$, where μ is the mobility (m²/V·s). Electrons are more mobile than holes: in silicon μn ≈ 1350 and μp ≈ 480 cm²/V·s.

narration.en: An electric field makes carriers drift. Their drift velocity is mobility times field, and electrons are more mobile than holes.
narration.kn: ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ವಾಹಕಗಳನ್ನು ಡ್ರಿಫ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಡ್ರಿಫ್ಟ್ ವೇಗ = ಚಲನಶೀಲತೆ × ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ; ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳ ಚಲನಶೀಲತೆ ರಂಧ್ರಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು.

say.en: An electric field makes carriers drift. Their drift velocity is mobility times field, and electrons are more mobile than holes. Drift: caused by an electric field.
say.kn: ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ವಾಹಕಗಳನ್ನು ಡ್ರಿಫ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಡ್ರಿಫ್ಟ್ ವೇಗ equals ಚಲನಶೀಲತೆ times ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ; ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳ ಚಲನಶೀಲತೆ ರಂಧ್ರಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು.

say.en: v d equals micro E.
micro n > micro p.
Apply a voltage across a bar of semiconductor. The field points from plus to minus.
Holes drift along the field and electrons drift against it. Both make current in the same direction: this is drift current.
Conductivity depends on how many carriers there are and how mobile they are.
Now no field. If carriers are crowded at one end, they spread out to the other end. This is diffusion current.
In silicon electrons are more mobile than holes: 1350 against 480 square centimetres per volt-second.

narration.en: On the board: Two ways carriers move.

say.en: On the board: Two ways carriers move.

narration.en: Drift: in a field carriers move with an average velocity vd = µE on top of their random thermal motion; electrons go against the field and holes along it. Diffusion: with no field, carriers crowded in one place spread out towards where there are fewer.
narration.kn: ಅಪವಾಹ: ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ವಾಹಕಗಳು vd = µE ಸರಾಸರಿ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದ ವಿರುದ್ಧ, ರಂಧ್ರ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ. ಪ್ರಸರಣ: ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ದಟ್ಟ ಭಾಗದಿಂದ ವಿರಳ ಭಾಗಕ್ಕೆ ಹರಡುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: If carriers are more crowded in one region than another, they spread out from high to low concentration even with no field. This flow is the *diffusion current*; it is proportional to the concentration gradient dn/dx. Diffusion is important at a p-n junction, where the carrier concentration changes sharply. The total current is the sum of drift and diffusion currents.

narration.en: Diffusion current flows from high to low carrier concentration, without any field. It is the key process at a p-n junction.
narration.kn: ವಿಸರಣ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಯಾವುದೇ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆಯಿಂದ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆಯ ಕಡೆ ಹರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. p-n ಸಂಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಇದು ಮುಖ್ಯ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆ.

say.en: Diffusion current flows from high to low carrier concentration, without any field. It is the key process at a p-n junction. Diffusion: caused by a concentration gradient.

say.en: Let us solve this together. n-type silicon has N D equals 10 to the power 16 centimetres to the power minus 3 and micro n equals 1350 square centimetres per volt s. Find a its resistivity and b the drift velocity and current density in a field of 100 volts per centimetre. (e equals 1.6 times 10 to the power minus 19 C; neglect holes).
sigma equals e N D micro n equals 1.6 times 10 to the power minus 19 times 10 to the power 16 times 1350 equals 2.16 S over cm.
rho equals 1/ sigma equals 1 over 2.16 is approximately 0.46 ohms cm.
v d equals micro n E equals 1350 times 100 equals 1.35 times 10 to the power 5 centimetres per second.
J equals sigma E equals 2.16 times 100 equals 216 A over cm squared.
So the answer is rho is approximately 0.46 ohms cm; v d equals 1.35 times 10 to the power 5 centimetres per second; J equals 216 A over cm squared.
